info.title: Judt API
info.description:
The Judt API creates and runs Apps. Each App has a sandbox, where you and agents edit and run its source, and a production deployment that serves it.

## Authentication

Send an API token or an OAuth access token in the `Authorization` header.

- **API token:** send it as a bearer token. A token belongs to one organization, and you create and revoke tokens in the dashboard. A token scoped to one App can reach only that App. An organization-wide token can also create a short-lived token for one App with `POST /api/tokens`, to give to an agent or an MCP client.
- **OAuth access token:** an agent gets one when a person approves its access to one organization, so the person never handles a token. Reads need the `apps:read` scope, and changes need `apps:write`. To register and sign in, follow https://judt.ai/auth.md. Send the token as a bearer token, or with a DPoP proof if it's bound to a DPoP key. One access token can work on both this API and the MCP server at https://api.judt.ai/mcp.

## Sandboxes

Creating an App reserves its address, but it doesn't start a sandbox or publish anything. There's no endpoint to start a sandbox. A request that needs the sandbox starts it first, so the first request after the sandbox goes idle takes longer. Files, Git, commands, commits, restores, previews, and deployments all need the sandbox.

The sandbox stops on its own when it's idle. If `sandbox_status` is `failed`, the most recent start failed, and the API retries it while the sandbox is needed.

## Pagination

A list returns one page at a time, in the form `{"results": [...], "has_more": true, "next_cursor": "CURSOR"}`. To get the next page, list again with `cursor` set to `next_cursor`, and the same `sort` and filters. Results that arrive while you page don't shift your pages. On the last page, `has_more` is `false`, and `next_cursor` still finds results added later.

## Retries

A request that creates, changes, or deletes something returns `200` after the work is done, with the resource as it is afterward. To retry a request safely, send an `Idempotency-Key` header. For 30 days, a retry with the same key and input returns the first request's result instead of repeating the work. If you don't send a key, the API generates one and returns it in the `Idempotency-Key` response header. Setting and deleting a Secret take no key, because repeating them changes nothing. A visitor token or a preview link is created fresh each time, because nothing is stored to repeat.

The API records file writes and deletes, commands, commits, and restores before it runs them. The response status tells you what to do next:

- `503` or `504`: the action is recorded but not finished. To get its result, retry with the same key. A new key would run the action again.
- `4xx` or `502`: the result is final. A retry with the same key returns the same response.

A `504 request_timeout` response says how far the work got and which event to check. The work continues, and a retry with the same key picks it up.

## Troubleshooting

To see what happened to an App's sandbox, deployments, and deletion, list its events with `GET /api/apps/{id}/events`. To see what the App's code did, including requests, output, exceptions, and failed builds, list its logs with `GET /api/apps/{id}/logs`.

## Time limits

Requests have the following time limits:

- Stopping the sandbox: 120 seconds.
- File writes, commits, and restores: 120 seconds.
- Commands: the command's `timeout_seconds`, up to 120 seconds, plus 60 seconds to stop it and save its result.
- Publishing, unpublishing, deleting an App, and changing production settings: 540 seconds, including any sandbox start.

If a file write, commit, restore, or command has to start the sandbox, it gets up to 120 more seconds.

## Errors

An error returns a JSON body in the form `{"error": {"code": "CODE", "message": "MESSAGE", "detail": "DETAIL", "request_id": "REQUEST_ID"}}`. The `code` value is stable, so check it rather than `message`. The `detail` value is optional. When a parameter or a body field isn't valid, the request returns `400 invalid_request`, `message` names the field, and `detail` lists every problem if there's more than one.

When the server rejects a credential, it returns a JSON error body and sets the `WWW-Authenticate` header. A `401` response includes the `resource_metadata` URL in `WWW-Authenticate` (RFC 9728):

| Status | Error code / header | Cause | Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `401` | `unauthenticated` | The request has no credential, or the API token or OAuth access token is invalid, expired, or revoked. | Send a valid API token or OAuth access token. |
| `401` | `invalid_token` | `WWW-Authenticate` error when an API token or OAuth access token is expired, revoked, or issued for a different `resource` audience. | Refresh the access token, or request a token for the target server. |
| `401` | `invalid_dpop_proof` | The `DPoP` proof header is missing, expired, replayed, or signed for a different HTTP method or URL. | Create a new DPoP proof for the request method and URL. |
| `403` | `insufficient_scope` | The OAuth token does not have the required scope (`apps:read` or `apps:write`). | Request authorization with the scope named in `WWW-Authenticate`. |
| `403` | `app_scoped_token` | An App-scoped API token called `POST /api/apps` or `POST /api/tokens`. | Use an organization-wide API token. |
| `403` | `api_token_required` | An OAuth access token called `POST /api/tokens`. | Use an organization-wide API token. |
| `403` | `sign_in_required` | A Personal Agent Session Token was used before the user signed in or after the user signed out. | Tell the user to sign in to the Session. |
| `403` | `forbidden` | Your organization role (`member`) does not allow this action. | Ask an organization `owner` or `admin` to do the action. |

get.description: Returns who the request acts as: the person, the organization that the credential reaches, the person's role in it, and the credential itself. Use it to check a credential, or to find out whether it reaches one App or all of them.

200.description: The person, organization, role, and credential.

post.description: Creates an App and reserves its address. The App's sandbox doesn't start, and nothing is published, until you use them. During the beta an organization can have 10 Apps.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A key that identifies this request for retries, up to 200 printable characters. A retry with the same key and input returns the first request's result instead of repeating the work. If you omit the key, the API generates one and returns it in the `Idempotency-Key` response header.

name.description: The App's display name, up to 100 characters.

slug.description: The App's label under the App base domain. If another App has the slug, including a deleted App, or the slug is reserved, the request returns `409 slug_unavailable`. Reserved slugs: `staging`, `preview`, `api`, `www`, `local`. If you omit it, the API generates one, such as `plucky-teal-tatooine`.

template_id.description: The ID of the template to create the App from. To list templates, use `GET /api/templates`. Default: the Hello template. An unknown ID returns `404 template_not_found`.

production.description: Who can reach the published App. Default: public.

visibility.description:
Who can reach the published App:
- `public`: anyone.
- `password`: anyone with the App's password, for 60 minutes at a time.
- `private`: members of the App's organization, who sign in through judt.

Access tokens open password-protected and private Apps. The sandbox is always private to the organization.

password.description: The App's password, 8 to 128 characters. It's required when `visibility` is `password`, and it's accepted only then. Setting a new password signs out every browser that used the old one. Responses never include the password.

Idempotency-Key.description: The key this request ran under: the one you sent, or one the API generated. To pick up the work after a timeout, retry with this key.

Idempotency-Retry-Window.description: How long you can retry with the same key, in seconds: 2592000 (30 days).

403.description:
- `app_scoped_token`: the request used an App-scoped token, which can't create Apps.
- `app_limit_reached`: the organization has 10 Apps, the beta limit. Delete one, or send feedback to ask for more.

409.description:
- `idempotency_conflict`: the key was used with a different request.
- `idempotency_expired`: the key is too old to reuse.

Creates a visitor token, which opens the published App for five minutes without its password or sign-in. To use it, send it in the `X-Judt-Access-Token` header, or add it to a link as the `access_token` URL parameter. A public App ignores the token.

post.description:
Creates an API token that reaches only one App, for up to 24 hours. Give it to an agent or an MCP client that should work on that App and nothing else. The token can't reach other Apps, create Apps, or create tokens. It stops working at `expires_at`, and never outlives the token that created it, so it can't extend that token's access.

Only an organization-wide API token can create one. The response is the only place the token's value appears, so store it before you continue. If the response is lost, retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`: the retry returns the same token with a new value, and the earlier value stops working. To revoke a token before it expires, use the dashboard.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: A key that identifies this request for retries, up to 200 printable characters. A retry with the same key and input returns the first request's result instead of repeating the work. If you omit the key, the API generates one and returns it in the `Idempotency-Key` response header.

name.description: A name for the token, up to 100 characters. The dashboard lists the token by this name.

app_id.description: The App that the token reaches. The token can't reach any other App or create Apps.

expires_in.description: How long the token works, in seconds, from 60 to 86400 (24 hours). Default: 3600. The token never outlives the token that created it.

200.description: The new token, with its value.

Idempotency-Key.description: The key this request ran under: the one you sent, or one the API generated. To pick up the work after a timeout, retry with this key.

Idempotency-Retry-Window.description: How long you can retry with the same key, in seconds: 2592000 (30 days).

- `api_token_required`: the request used an OAuth access token. Use an organization-wide API token.

If a waiting agent turn requested this Secret, and it's the last one that the turn needs, the turn resumes.

get.description:
Lists the App's source files by path: the files Git tracks, and new files that `.gitignore` doesn't ignore. Folders aren't listed separately. A file's path includes its folders.

To find code, filter paths with `path` or `glob`, and file text with `content` or `pattern`. A text search adds `match_count` and the first 20 matching lines to each file. To see more of a file, read it with `lines`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A unique ID that starts with `app_`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of files to return.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Where to start: the `next_cursor` of the page before, listed with the same `sort`. Without it, the list starts with the first files.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: A comma-separated list of fields to sort by: `path` or `size`. Each field sorts ascending. To sort a field descending, prefix it with `-`. Ties are sorted by `path`.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Returns only files whose `path` contains this text, ignoring case.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: Returns only files whose `content` contains this text, ignoring case.

parameters.name: glob
parameters.description: Returns only files whose `path` matches this glob, from the App's root. `*` matches within one folder, `**` matches across folders, `?` matches one character, `[abc]` matches one of a set, and `{ts,tsx}` matches any of its alternatives, as in `src/**/*.{ts,tsx}`. Without a leading `**/`, a glob matches only from the root: `*.json` matches `package.json` but not `src/data.json`.

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Returns only files with a line that this regular expression matches, in Perl syntax. Matching is case-sensitive; to ignore case, start the expression with `(?i)`. Can't be combined with `content`.

400.description:
- `invalid_request`: a parameter is malformed, or the request sets both `content` and `pattern`.
- `invalid_pattern`: `glob` or `pattern` isn't valid, and `detail` says why.

502.description: The sandbox returned a response that the API can't use, such as `sandbox_incompatible` or `helper_output_too_large`. Retrying doesn't change the result.

get.description:
Returns the file as JSON. For a text file, `content` holds the text, and `line_count` says how many lines it has. To read only some lines, set `lines`. For a binary file, `binary` is `true` and `content` is left out. To get the bytes, send `Accept: application/octet-stream`.

The `ETag` header holds the whole file's version, even when you read only some lines. To skip an unchanged file, send its ETag in `If-None-Match`, and the request returns `304`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A unique ID that starts with `app_`.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The file's path from the App's root, such as `src/lib/util.ts`.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: One or more quoted ETags from earlier reads. If the file still matches one of them, the request returns `304` with no body.

parameters.name: lines
parameters.description: Returns only these lines of a text file: a range such as `120-180`, a start such as `120-` (to the end), or one line such as `120`. Lines are numbered from 1, and both ends are inclusive. An end past the last line stops at the last line.

200.description: The file, as JSON or as raw bytes.

ETag.description: The file's version: its quoted SHA-256 hash.

400.description:
- `invalid_request`: `lines` is malformed, or it's set with `Accept: application/octet-stream`.
- `line_out_of_range`: `lines` starts past the file's last line.
- `binary_file`: `lines` is set for a binary file.

502.description: The sandbox returned a response that the API can't use, such as `sandbox_incompatible` or `helper_output_too_large`. Retrying doesn't change the result.

put.description:
Creates or replaces a file, up to 1 MiB, and creates any missing folders. Send text as JSON, in the form `{"content": "TEXT"}`, or send raw bytes with any other `Content-Type`.

To replace only a specific version, send its ETag in `If-Match`. To create the file only if it doesn't exist, send `If-None-Match: *`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A unique ID that starts with `app_`.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The file's path from the App's root, such as `src/lib/util.ts`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: One or more quoted ETags from earlier reads, or `*`. The request runs only if the file matches one of the ETags, or, for `*`, if the file exists. Otherwise, it returns `412`.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: `*` to create the file only if it doesn't exist. If the file exists, the request returns `412`.
